newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares suffer from fuel shortage.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares suffer from fuel shortage.

text.p: Shares of oil marketing companies on Thursday received the cold shoulder from brokers as the latest fuel scarcity in oil-producing Nigeria worsened, traders said.
The all-share index, however, rose to 8336.91 from 8270.04 on Wednesday.
Oil shares, usually the toast of the market, stayed mostly frozen except for token positive movements by two oil firms.
"This scarcity disrupts businesses with serious effect on the economy," said one dealer, adding "It is a good thing to shun the the oil shares today."
For unexplained reasons, African Petroleum rose five kobo to 58.75 naira while National Oil was 61.80 naira, up nine kobo.
The dearest stock on the exchange, Unipetrol, was unchanged at 76.00 naira, just as Total which was 73.05 naira. Mobil closed at 63.50 naira, Texaco 45.06 naira and Agip 27.40 naira.
Nigerian Bottling Company led food and beverages stocks with a 70 kobo gain to 50.00 naira on growing demand.
West African Portland Cement Company, the leader in its group, soared to 63.00 naira, up 50 kobo.

There was increased interest in bank shares also, causing them to finish stronger. First Bank rose 37 kobo to 17.40 naira, Union Bank, with 40 kobo, closed at 15.00 naira and UBA rose 30 kobo to 13.00 naira.

Stationery company Tripple Gee was down 10 kobo at 5.20 naira, Cement Company of Northern Nigeria down three kobo at 2.91 naira, Afprint four kobo lower at 2.15 naira and African Paints two kobo weaker at 1.38 naira because investors were selling them.
